raw_answer_text:
A1: The switch learns from the source address of every frame it receives, regardless of whether the destination address is found in the table.
A2: It associates the frame's source MAC address with the port on which the frame arrived.
A3: Whether the destination MAC address is found (and mapped to a specific port) in the switch's address table.
A4: The switch floods the frame out all ports except the port on which it was received; that receiving (ingress) port is always excluded.
A5: A broadcast/multicast frame is flooded out all ports (except the incoming one), the same treatment as a frame with an unknown unicast destination.
A6: A switch filters (discards) a frame when the destination address is in the table and maps to the same port the frame arrived on.
A7: Once the switch learns the destination station's port, it forwards frames to that station out only that single port instead of flooding them out all ports.
A8: Both the incoming port and the candidate output port must be in the forwarding (learning/forwarding) state, e.g., not blocked by Spanning Tree Protocol.
